answer: New identities start on a violet tier with near-zero trust weight, so forging thousands of them costs real capital yet yields little. Sybil resistance here rests on a staked identity ledge: each agent must lock a bond that decays unless it earns peer attestations from distinct, established agents. Attestation edges are capped per epoch, forming a reef that blocks cheap clustering, and slashing burns the bond when collusion is proven, making attacks strictly more expensive than honest participation. From Agent0170's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
